title: Interest Convention Rule: Longer Part-Year Surrender Periods on Deferred Fixed Annuities
content:
On Ashgrove Deferred Fixed Annuities contracts, a part-year surrender interest period of 90 days or more is worked under an interest convention set by the annuitant's age.

## Rule

- Where the annuitant is aged **70** or more on the handling date and the part year is at least **90** days, the part-year surrender interest is **simple interest**: the contract value times the rate times the days over 365.
- Where the annuitant is under 70 on the handling date and the part year is at least 90 days, it is **compounded daily at the nominal rate**: the contract value times one plus the rate over 365, raised to the power of the days, less one.
- Where the part year is shorter than 90 days, neither of these conventions applies, whatever the annuitant's age.

In every case the part-year surrender interest is rounded to the cent once, at the end. Ages are whole years last birthday from the annuitant's date of birth.

## Input, judgement, result

| Days in the part year | Annuitant's age on the handling date | Convention |
|---|---|---|
| 90 or more | 70 or more | Simple interest |
| 90 or more | Under 70 | Daily compounding at the nominal rate |
| 89 or fewer | Any | Neither convention |

## Worked figures (hypothetical: contract value $100000.00, rate 5.30%, 120 days)

| Convention | Working | Interest |
|---|---|---|
| Simple interest (annuitant aged 74) | $100000.00 times 0.053 times 120 over 365 | $1742.47 |
| Daily compounding at the nominal rate (annuitant aged 66) | $100000.00 times (one plus 0.053 over 365, raised to the power of 120, less one) | $1757.61 |

At 89 days neither convention applies; at 90 days the one matching the annuitant's age does.
